summary.short: The National Security and Investment Act 2021 lets the Secretary of State review acquisitions of control over UK entities and assets that may raise national security risks. It requires mandatory notification of notifiable acquisitions, which are void without approval, and allows call-in notices, interim and final orders, and monetary penalties and offences.
summary.long: The Act creates a national security review regime for acquisitions of control over UK qualifying entities (any non-individual entity) and qualifying assets (including land, ideas and information such as databases, source code and algorithms). The Secretary of State may give a call-in notice where a trigger event (gaining control under ss.8-9) may give rise to a national security risk, within 6 months of becoming aware of it and 5 years of the event (s.2). Notifiable acquisitions require a mandatory notice before completion and are void without approval (ss.13-14), with a 30-working-day review period; voluntary notices are also possible (s.18). The assessment period has an initial 30 working days, extendable by 45 working days (s.23). Information and attendance notices (ss.19-20), interim orders (s.25) and final orders (s.26) may be made, and final orders can reach persons outside the UK in defined cases. The Act also provides financial assistance (s.30), CMA coordination (s.31), offences with imprisonment up to 5 years on indictment (s.39), civil monetary penalties capped at the higher of 5% of turnover and £10 million (s.41), cost recovery, appeals within 28 days (ss.49-51), information-sharing gateways (ss.54-55) and an annual report (s.61).

obligations.summary: Where financial assistance under section 30 totals 100 million pounds or more in a relevant period, the Secretary of State must lay a report of the amount before the House of Commons, and report further amounts in subsequent periods.
obligations.conditional_on: Financial assistance under section 30 totals GBP 100 million or more in a relevant period

evidence.quote: the Secretary of State must as soon as practicable lay a report of the amount before the House of Commons.

obligations.summary: Before giving a direction to the CMA under section 31, the Secretary of State must consult the CMA and other appropriate persons; the direction must be published.
obligations.conditional_on: Final order or final notification in force for a merger-type trigger event and Secretary of State gives a direction under section 31(2)

evidence.quote: Before giving a direction under this section, the Secretary of State must consult the CMA

obligations.summary: The CMA must comply with a direction under section 31 regardless of any other duty imposed on it.
obligations.conditional_on: Direction given by the Secretary of State under section 31(2)

evidence.quote: The duty of the CMA to comply with a direction given under this section applies regardless of any other duty imposed on the CMA.

obligations.summary: A public authority or overseas public authority receiving information disclosed under section 54(2) or (3) may not use it for another purpose or further disclose it, except with Secretary of State consent.
obligations.conditional_on: Information received under section 54(2) or (3)

evidence.quote: use the information for a purpose other than the purpose for which it was disclosed

obligations.summary: Before disclosing information under section 54, the Secretary of State must consider whether disclosure would unreasonably prejudice the commercial interests of any person; for disclosure to an overseas authority it must have regard to self-incrimination protection and seriousness.
obligations.conditional_on: Secretary of State considers disclosing information under section 54

evidence.quote: the Secretary of State must consider whether the disclosure would prejudice, to an unreasonable degree, the commercial interests of any person concerned.

obligations.summary: A person who receives information disclosed by HMRC under section 54 may not use it for a purpose other than the purpose in section 54(1) or further disclose it, except with HMRC consent.
obligations.conditional_on: Information disclosed by HMRC under section 54

evidence.quote: use the information for a purpose other than the purpose mentioned in section 54(1)

obligations.summary: The Competition and Markets Authority must give the Secretary of State such information in its possession and such assistance as the Secretary of State reasonably directs to enable exercise of functions under the Act.
obligations.conditional_on: Direction by the Secretary of State

evidence.quote: The Competition and Markets Authority must give the Secretary of State—

obligations.summary: For each relevant period the Secretary of State must prepare an annual report with the listed details (financial assistance, notice counts, sectors, orders) and lay it before each House of Parliament.
obligations.conditional_on: End of each relevant period

evidence.quote: lay a copy of it before each House of Parliament as soon as is practicable after the end of that period.

obligations.summary: Secretary of State may make notifiable acquisition regulations specifying notifiable acquisitions; such regulations are subject to the affirmative procedure under section 63(5).

obligations.summary: Secretary of State may by regulations amend the list of assets excluded from control of assets, and prescribe other circumstances in which a person is not treated as gaining control of a qualifying asset; affirmative procedure applies.

evidence.quote: The Secretary of State may by regulations prescribe the form and content of a mandatory notice.

obligations.summary: Secretary of State may by regulations alter the percentage used in the permitted maximum monetary penalties under section 41(1) and (2), and amend the sums in section 41(1) to (7); affirmative procedure applies under section 63(5).

evidence.quote: amend subsection (1) or (2) so as to alter the percentage for the time being specified there

obligations.summary: Secretary of State may by regulations make provision for the procedure for giving or serving notices, orders and documents under the Act.

enforcement.authority: Courts (summary conviction or conviction on indictment), following prosecution by the Director of Public Prosecutions (s. 37)
enforcement.triggered_by: Offence under s. 32 (completing a notifiable acquisition without approval) or s. 33 (failing to comply with an interim or final order); officers may also be liable under s. 36
enforcement.max_penalty_text: On conviction on indictment: imprisonment for a term not exceeding 5 years, or a fine (or both). Summary conviction: imprisonment up to the magistrates' court general limit (England and Wales), 12 months (Scotland) or 6 months (Northern Ireland), or a fine (or both)
enforcement.penalty_formula: Fine amount not specified in the text for this sanction

evidence.quote: on conviction on indictment, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 5 years, or a fine (or both)

enforcement.authority: Courts (summary conviction or conviction on indictment), following prosecution by the Director of Public Prosecutions (s. 37)
enforcement.triggered_by: Offence under s. 34 (information and attendance of witnesses, including supplying false or misleading information) or s. 35 (use or disclosure of information in contravention of s. 54 or 55(1))
enforcement.max_penalty_text: On conviction on indictment: imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years, or a fine (or both). Summary conviction: imprisonment up to the magistrates' court general limit (England and Wales), 12 months (Scotland) or 6 months (Northern Ireland), or a fine (or both)
enforcement.penalty_formula: Fine amount not specified in the text for this sanction

evidence.quote: on conviction on indictment, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years, or a fine (or both)

enforcement.triggered_by: Offence under s. 32 (completing a notifiable acquisition without approval), s. 33 (failing to comply with an interim or final order) or s. 34(1)(c)-(3) and (4)-type information offences as listed in s. 40(1)(a)-(c); monetary penalty imposed by penalty notice only where satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that the offence was committed
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Fixed penalty for s. 32 or s. 33 offences: the higher of 5% of total turnover of the business and £10 million (business); £10 million (otherwise). Daily rate penalty for s. 33 offences: the higher of 0.1% of total turnover and £200,000 per day (business); £200,000 per day (otherwise)
enforcement.penalty_formula: Fixed penalty for a business: the higher of 5% of the total value of the turnover of the business (in and outside the UK, including owned or controlled businesses) and £10 million; daily rate for s. 33 offences by a business: the higher of 0.1% of total turnover and £200,000. Amount set by the Secretary of State up to these maxima (s. 40(6))
enforcement.cure_period: None stated in text; the Secretary of State must have regard to the possibility and desirability of rectifying the failure and steps taken to rectify it (s. 40(7)(c)-(d))

evidence.quote: the higher of 5% of the total value of the turnover of the business

enforcement.triggered_by: Offence under s. 34(1)(a) (failing to comply with an information notice or attendance notice), s. 34(1)(b), s. 34(2), s. 34(3) or s. 34(4) (information offences)
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Fixed penalty up to £30,000; daily rate penalty up to £15,000 per day for s. 34(1)(a) offences
enforcement.penalty_formula: Fixed penalty maximum £30,000 (s. 34(1)(a), (1)(b), (2), (3) or (4)); daily rate maximum £15,000 per day (s. 34(1)(a)); combination of fixed and daily rate permitted for s. 34(1)(a) (s. 40(4))
enforcement.cure_period: None stated in text; the Secretary of State must have regard to the possibility and desirability of rectifying the failure (s. 40(7)(c))

evidence.quote: The permitted maximum fixed penalty for an offence under section 34(1)(a) is £30,000.

enforcement.triggered_by: Offence under s. 34(1)(a) (daily rate penalty for failing to comply with an information or attendance notice)
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Daily rate penalty up to £15,000 per day
enforcement.penalty_formula: Daily rate maximum £15,000 per day for s. 34(1)(a); accumulation runs from the day after the penalty notice until the requirement is satisfied or no longer applies (s. 40(9))

evidence.quote: The permitted maximum amount per day for a daily rate penalty for an offence under section 34(1)(a) is £15,000.

enforcement.authority: High Court (England and Wales or Northern Ireland) or Court of Session (Scotland), on civil proceedings brought by the Secretary of State
enforcement.triggered_by: Failure to comply with a requirement under an information notice, attendance notice, interim order or final order
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Injunction, specific performance of a statutory duty under s. 45 of the Court of Session Act 1988, or any other appropriate relief or remedy; no amount stated
enforcement.penalty_formula: Not applicable (civil relief, no amount stated)
